theory.title: Personality, motivation and behavioural patterns
theory.explanation: Analyse dispositions without reducing people to labels; explain how motivation, goals, incentives and context interact. C1 communication requires nuanced generalisations, precise distinctions and evidence-aware conclusions.

reading.english:
Personality and the Limits of Labels

Personality frameworks can help describe recurring patterns, but they become misleading when treated as complete explanations of behaviour. A person who is generally conscientious may still miss a deadline when competing demands become overwhelming. Someone who appears reserved in a formal meeting may be highly expressive among close friends. Context does not erase individual differences; it reveals how dispositions interact with expectations, incentives and circumstances.

Motivation is similarly complex. Intrinsic interest can sustain engagement, yet external rewards may be useful when a task is repetitive or difficult. The distinction is not simply between good and bad motives. Rather, the effect of an incentive depends on how it is experienced and whether it supports or undermines a person's sense of autonomy. Self-efficacy also matters: people are more likely to persist when they believe their actions can make a difference.

A useful account of behaviour therefore avoids reducing people to labels. It asks what goals they pursue, what constraints they face and how their priorities change. Traits can suggest tendencies, but they do not determine every choice.
reading.spanish: La personalidad y los límites de las etiquetas. El texto analiza cómo los rasgos interactúan con el contexto y cómo los incentivos, la autonomía y la autoeficacia influyen en la motivación.

listening.english: People are often described in terms of stable personality traits, yet behaviour changes with context. Intrinsic motivation may sustain interest, while external incentives can help with repetitive tasks. Self-efficacy influences whether people believe effort will make a difference. When goals are realistic and personally meaningful, individuals may be more willing to persist. Even so, motivation is affected by competing priorities, available support and the possibility of setbacks. A useful assessment therefore considers both personal dispositions and the conditions in which behaviour occurs.
